intro: The Spanish of the screen: devices, actions, problems, and how to say what happens by accident.
p.archivo.consejo: The ch sounds as in «chico»: «ar-CHI-bo». It is also the place where old documents are kept.
p.carpeta.consejo: It is used for paper and for computers alike: «una carpeta con documentos».
p.pantalla.consejo: The ll sounds like y: «pan-TA-ya». You say «pantalla táctil» and «pantalla completa».
p.teclado.consejo: It comes from «tecla». There are also piano and phone keyboards.
p.ratón.consejo: It is also the small animal. The first r is strong: «rra-TON». You say «mover el ratón».
p.enlace.consejo: You also say «vínculo». «Pinchar en el enlace» is clicking on it.
p.pinchar.consejo: It takes «en»: «pinchar en el enlace». It also means to prick with something sharp, like a needle.
p.arrastrar.consejo: It has two r sounds in a row: «a-rras-TRAR». It also means to pull something along the floor.
p.contraseña.consejo: It is written with ñ. You say «poner una contraseña» and «olvidar la contraseña».
p.configurar.consejo: It is regular. It comes from «configuración» and is used with devices and programs.
p.reiniciar.consejo: It has «re-» (again): «iniciar» and «reiniciar». The stress is on the last syllable: «rrei-ni-THYAR».
p.bloquearse.consejo: You also say «colgarse». With «se me»: «se me ha bloqueado el ordenador».
p.copia de seguridad.consejo: You say «hacer una copia de seguridad». You also hear «backup» in English.
p.actualizar.consejo: It comes from «actual». The z of «actualizar» sounds «th»: «ak-twa-li-THAR».
b1.texto:
**The device.** The ordenador (in Latin America, la computadora) has a **pantalla**, a **teclado** and a **ratón**. An **archivo** lives in a **carpeta**.

**What you do.** You **pinchas en** a **enlace**, **arrastras** a file into a folder, **configuras** a program and **actualizas** the system. To log in you need a **contraseña**.

**Problems.** If the computer **se bloquea**, you **reinicias** it. To lose nothing, you make a **copia de seguridad**.

**By accident.** When something happens by accident, we use **se + me/te/le**: **Se me ha borrado el archivo.** The verb agrees with what gets deleted: **Se me han borrado las fotos.**

**Instructions with usted.** The technician gives orders: **Pinche**, **mantenga**, **reinicie**. With **hasta que** and the future, the verb goes in the subjunctive.
b2.f2.texto: Hold the button down until the screen goes off.
b2.f3.texto: Now it asks me for a password that I do not remember.
b2.f4.texto: Click on the link and type a new password.
b2.f5.texto: Do I have to set anything else up?
b2.f6.texto: You must make a backup every week.
b4.texto:
**Se + me/te/le + verb** tells something that happens by accident. The person affected goes in **me, te, le, nos, os, les**; the verb agrees with what happens: **Se me ha borrado el archivo. Se me han borrado las fotos.**

**Formal commands.** The present subjunctive is used: **Pinche**, **mantenga**, **reinicie**. Verbs in **-ar** end in **-e**; verbs in **-er** and **-ir**, in **-a**: **escriba**, **abra**.

**Hasta que + subjunctive** when you talk about the future: **Espere hasta que se cargue la página.**
b4.e0.texto: The file got deleted on me.
b4.e1.texto: Restart the computer and update the system.
b5.f0.texto: The laptop screen stays still and blue, like a frozen lake.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía presses the keys again and again with nervous fingers.
b5.f2.texto: The fan buzzes on the desk like a tired insect.
b5.f3.texto: At the window, the rain taps the glass with small cold fingers.
b5.f4.texto: She breathes deeply, closes her eyes and counts to ten.
b5.f5.texto: With a steady finger she keeps the power button pressed.
b5.f6.texto: A thick silence suddenly fills the whole room.
b5.f7.texto: Ten endless seconds go by, like a summer afternoon.
b5.f8.texto: Then a white logo appears in the centre of the black screen.
b5.f9.texto: Lucía smiles with relief and finally saves the file in the cloud.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «A propósito» is the opposite of by accident.
b6.o1: Se me ha borrado el archivo
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «se me» tells something that happens by accident.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence says it happened by accident?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «las fotos» is plural, so the verb is plural.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Las fotos» is plural; «ha» would not agree.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «He» goes with «yo», but the subject is «las fotos».
b8.frase: Tienes que actualizar el sistema y reiniciar el ordenador
b8.traduccion: You have to update the system and restart the computer
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Reiniciar» is turning a device off and on again.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Configurar» is adjusting how a program works.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «arrastrar» is moving something across the screen without letting go.
b9.pregunta: What do you do to move a file with the mouse?
b11.frase: Mantenga el botón hasta que se ____ la pantalla.
b11.o0.refuerzo: That is indicative; for the future you need the subjunctive.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «hasta que» + subjunctive when it has not happened yet.
b11.o2.refuerzo: After «hasta que» the future is not used.
b11.pregunta: Which form does «hasta que» take about the future?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it is a copy of your files in case of disaster.
b12.o1.refuerzo: A link takes you to another page; it saves nothing.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is a device, not a copy of your files.
b12.pregunta: What do you keep in case something fails?
p.ayudarle.consejo: «Le» here is the polite «you»: «ayudarle» means to help you formally.
p.bloqueado.consejo: Past participle of «bloquear»; a frozen screen is «bloqueado».
p.ordenador.consejo: In Spain «ordenador» means computer; in Latin America it is «computadora».
p.mantenga.consejo: Subjunctive of «mantener», a formal instruction: keep it.
p.pulsado.consejo: Past participle of «pulsar», to press a button.
p.pinche.consejo: Formal command of «pinchar», to click a link on screen.
p.escriba.consejo: Subjunctive of «escribir» in a formal instruction: type.
p.borrado.consejo: Participle of «borrar»; it goes after a form of «haber».
p.sistema.consejo: «Sistema» is the operating system of a computer.
p.cargue.consejo: Subjunctive of «cargar» after «hasta que», for a future moment.
p.portátil.consejo: A «portátil» is a laptop: it can be carried, from «portar».
p.pulsa.consejo: Third person of «pulsar», to press, in the present.
p.teclas.consejo: Plural of «tecla», a key on a keyboard or piano.
p.mantiene.consejo: Third person of «mantener» in the present.
p.espeso.consejo: «Espeso» describes something thick, like honey or fog.
p.logotipo.consejo: A «logotipo» is the symbol that identifies a brand.
